question: How do initialization seed, identity split seed, and channel-width variant affect identity-disjoint SurvFace verification and full-INT8 export quality?
objective: supervised contrastive loss with a 64-dimensional feature head
architecture_ablation: tiny uses the same objective, feature dimension, data split, batch composition, augmentation, and training seeds as base; only channel widths change
split_method: identity-disjoint 80/20 split stratified by image-count decile
cap_extension_rule: After initial training, resume any run that reached epoch 30 with fewer than five epochs since its last validation-AUC improvement to a total target of epoch 40. This is a continuation of the same run, not an additional independent seed; retain its full history and report the cap extension explicitly.
cap_extension_rule_addendum_2026_10_22: For runs resumed to epoch 40 that still reach the new cap with fewer than five no-improvement epochs, continue the same run to a total target of epoch 50 so the predeclared patience rule can stop it. This post-hoc continuation is reported separately and does not add independent seeds.
selection_and_test_policy: Checkpoint selection and thresholds use validation pairs only. Every exported candidate is evaluated on its own identity-disjoint validation pairs. Do not open the supplied SurvFace final pair annotations or Olivetti during this campaign; the final annotations were used once for the historical baseline and are not reused for selection.
interpretation_caveats: Best-epoch metrics on the validation set are subject to checkpoint-selection optimism.
Pair-bootstrap intervals treat pairs as independent and can be optimistic because images and identities recur across pairs.
The five-seed distribution estimates training-run variability on a fixed split; two split seeds provide only limited evidence about identity-split sensitivity.
The primary second-split group uses distinct training seeds; a supplemental matched-seed split-sensitivity campaign is predeclared separately.
The historical five-seed pilot used 12 intra-op and 2 inter-op threads; the predeclared 15-job campaign uses 4 intra-op and 1 inter-op thread for every job. Report those as separate cohorts.

evaluation.format: float TFLite and full signed-integer INT8 TFLite
